doc.title: Wikinews: Spanish midfielder Iniesta retires from international football
doc.abstract: Yesterday, Spanish footballer Andrés Iniesta announced retirement from international football. The midfielder made the announcement after Spain lost to Russia in the Last 16 match of the FIFA World Cup.

doc.title: Wikinews: FIFA World Cup 2018 Last 16: France, Uruguay send Argentina, Portugal home
doc.abstract: On Saturday, France defeated Argentina 4–3 and Uruguay defeated Portugal 2–1 in the FIFA football World Cup in the Last 16 knockout phase. France is scheduled to play against Uruguay for the quarter-finals.

doc.title: Wikinews: FIFA World Cup 2018 Last 16: Russia, Croatia beat Spain, Denmark in penalties
doc.abstract: On Sunday, Spain lost to Russia 4–3 in the penalty shootout while Croatia defeated Denmark 3–2 in the penalty shootout in the FIFA football World Cup in the Last 16 knockout phase. Both the matches were 1–1 at the end of added time.

doc.title: Wikinews: English football: Mohamed Salah signs contract extension with Liverpool
doc.abstract: Yesterday, English football club Liverpool announced the contract extension of Egyptian forward Mohamed Salah via their official website. The new "long-term" contract runs through 2023.

doc.title: Wikinews: Dublin Pride 2018 attracts tens of thousands of people
doc.abstract: On Saturday, the Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender (LGBT) Pride in the Irish capital Dublin attracted a record number of people. According to the organisers of the Pride, about 60 thousand people attended the event, almost double the number of attendees in last year's Pride.

doc.title: Wikinews: FIFA World Cup 2018 Last 16: Brazil, Belgium advance at expense of Mexico, Japan
doc.abstract: On Monday, Brazil defeated Mexico 2–0 and Belgium defeated Japan 3–2 in the FIFA football World Cup in the Last 16 knockout phase. Brazil is now scheduled to play Belgium in the quarter-finals.

doc.title: Wikinews: FIFA World Cup 2018 Last 16: Sweden, England knock out Switzerland, Colombia
doc.abstract: On Tuesday, Sweden defeated Switzerland 1–0 and England defeated Colombia 4–3 on penalties in the FIFA football World Cup in the Last 16 knockout phase. Sweden is now scheduled to play England in the quarter-finals.

doc.title: Wikinews: In Pictures: Helsinki Pride 2018 ends after record number of attendees
doc.abstract: On Sunday, the annual lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (LGBT) came to an end. According to organisers and police in the Finnish capital Helsinki, an estimated 100 thousand people attended the Saturday march of the Pride, which ran from June 25 to July 1 — about thrice the number of attendees of last year's Pride.

doc.title: Wikinews: FIFA World Cup 2018 quarterfinals: France, Belgium beat Uruguay, Brazil
doc.abstract: On Friday, France defeated Uruguay 2–0 in the FIFA football World Cup quarter-finals and Brazil lost 1–2 against Belgium. With this defeat only countries from the Confederation are now remaining in the tournament.

doc.title: Wikinews: French football: Gianluigi Buffon signs one-year contract with Paris SG
doc.abstract: Today, French-capital football club Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) announced the signing of Italian goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon on a one-year contract and an option for one additional season.

doc.title: Wikinews: France: Rainbow pedestrian crossings 'will be permanent!', Paris mayor says
doc.abstract: On Wednesday, Paris mayor announced via Twitter that the rainbow-coloured crossings in the French capital are to be made permanent. This move comes after multiple vandalisations of rainbow-coloured crossroads during this year's Paris Pride.

doc.title: Wikinews: FIFA World Cup 2018 quarterfinals: England beats Sweden, Croatia knocks out hosts Russia
doc.abstract: On Saturday, England defeated Sweden 2–0 in the FIFA football World Cup quarter-finals and the hosts Russia lost to Croatia 3–4 on penalties. Croatia are to play England for the spot in the finals.

doc.title: Wikinews: FIFA World Cup 2018 semifinals: Umtiti scores only goal, France reaches finals beating Belgium
doc.abstract: On Tuesday, France defeated Belgium 1–0 in the FIFA football World Cup semifinals. scored the only goal of the match, and France is to play Croatia in the final.

doc.title: Wikinews: Spanish Football Federation appoints Luis Enrique as men's national team coach
doc.abstract: On Monday, the (Royal Spanish Football Federation; RFEF) announced Luis Enrique as the new coach of the Spanish men's national football team. Per the contract, Enrique is to serve as the coach for two years.

doc.title: Wikinews: Football: Cristiano Ronaldo leaves Real Madrid for Juventus
doc.abstract: On Tuesday via their official website, Italian football club Juventus announced signing Portuguese forward Cristiano Ronaldo from Spanish capital club Real Madrid. Per the press release, Ronaldo penned a four-year contract with the club, which runs until June 30, 2022.

doc.title: Wikinews: Football: Manchester City signs Riyad Mahrez from Leicester
doc.abstract: On Tuesday, via their official website, Manchester City announced signing Algerian footballer from for a fee of 60 million , making him the most expensive player in Man City's history. Mahrez signed a five-year contract with the English winners which runs through 2023.

doc.title: Wikinews: London Pride organisers apologise after protestors interrupt parade
doc.abstract: On Sunday, Pride in London organisers issued a public apology via their website condemning an unregistered lesbian protest group as "transphobic, hateful protestors who blocked the Pride". The annual lesbian, gay, transgender and bisexual (LGBT) Pride in the English capital ended with roughly 30 thousand people participating in this year's parade, organisers said.

doc.title: Wikinews: FIFA World Cup 2018 semifinals: Croatia sends England home, 2-1
doc.abstract: On Wednesday, Croatia defeated England 2–1 in the semi-final of the 2018 FIFA Football World Cup with Mario Mandžukić scoring the winning goal in the additional time. With this victory, Croatia is in their first-ever FIFA World Cup finals, and they are to face France on Sunday.

doc.title: Wikinews: Swiss footballer Xherdan Shaqiri joins Liverpool
doc.abstract: Yesterday, Swiss footballer Xherdan Shaqiri joined Liverpool FC on a "long-term contract", the club announced via their official website. According to multiple reports, Liverpool exercised the 13 million release clause in his contract with .

doc.title: Wikinews: English football: Chelsea announces Maurizio Sarri as their head coach
doc.abstract: Yesterday, English football club Chelsea FC announced signing as the club's new coach. The Italian coach has signed a three-year contract with the London-based club.

doc.title: Wikinews: FIFA World Cup 2018: Belgium beats England 2-0 to claim third place finish
doc.abstract: On Saturday, Belgium defeated England 2–0 in the third-place match of the 2018 FIFA Football World Cup. Thomas Meunier scored an early goal and Eden Hazard doubled the lead for Belgium in the 82nd minute to seal off the third place at the tournament.

doc.title: Wikinews: France beats Croatia 4-2 to win 2018 FIFA World Cup
doc.abstract: Yesterday, France defeated Croatia 4–2 in the final of 2018 FIFA Football World Cup to win the tournament for the second time. French teenager became the second teenager to score in a FIFA World Cup final after did in 1958's tournament.

doc.title: Wikinews: US astronomers announce discovering ten tiny Jovian satellites
doc.abstract: On Tuesday, astronomers of the in Washington, DC, United States, announced the discovery of ten small satellites orbiting Jupiter. With this discovery, Jupiter now has 79 known satellites.

doc.title: Wikinews: Indian Supreme Court: unconstitutional to bar women of certain age group from entering Sabarimala temple
doc.abstract: On Wednesday, the Indian Supreme Court declared that preventing women of age 10–50 from entering the in Kerala was "arbitrary" and unconstitutional.

doc.title: Wikinews: Israeli Knesset passes 'Jewish nation-state' bill
doc.abstract: On Thursday, the Israeli parliament, the Knesset, passed the "Jewish nation-state" bill granting Israel the status of "national home of the Jewish people". Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called it "a defining moment in the annals of and the history of the state of Israel".

doc.title: Wikinews: After signing peace declarations, Eritrea reopens embassy in Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa
doc.abstract: On Monday, Eritrea reopened their embassy in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa just a week after both the countries signed a declaration of the end of the two-decade-long conflict between the countries.

doc.title: Wikinews: Hindi poet and songwriter Gopal Das Neeraj dies, aged 93
doc.abstract: Yesterday, poet and songwriter died at the in Delhi, India. The poet was 93-years-old.

doc.title: Wikinews: Cretaceous baby snake fossil found in Myanmar
doc.abstract: A team of researchers from China, Canada, the United States, and Australia published on Wednesday their discovery of an early fossilized baby snake, reportedly the oldest ever found, in a piece of amber in the middle of a deposit in Myanmar. The findings appeared in the journal .

doc.title: Wikinews: US director James Gunn fired from Marvel Studios for decade-old offensive tweets
doc.abstract: On Friday, US director and screenwriter was fired from work on for reportedly for his offensive tweets from 2008 to 2011 about, amongst other things, rape and .

doc.title: Wikinews: German footballer Mesut Özil announces retirement from international football over 'racism'
doc.abstract: On Sunday, German footballer Mesut Özil announced retiring from international football via his official Twitter handle. The 29-year-old gave racism as the reason for his retirement.

doc.title: Wikinews: Palestine elected as G-77's presiding country, ambassador Riyad Mansour confirms
doc.abstract: On Tuesday, Riyad Mansour, Palestine's ambassador to the United Nations, confirmed Palestine would preside next year over the UN's bloc of developing countries.

doc.title: Wikinews: First-ever Dublin Trans Pride attracts hundreds
doc.abstract: On Saturday, hundreds of people reportedly attended the first-ever Transgender Pride in the Irish capital Dublin. Different from last month's Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender (LGBT) Pride, this Pride focused on issues concerning transgender people.

doc.title: Wikinews: Total lunar eclipse occurs in July 2018
doc.abstract: On Friday–Saturday —depending on observer's timezone— a total lunar eclipse occurred as the Moon was in the shadow of the Earth. As normal during such an eclipse, the Moon became faint and turned completely red as bluer light was by the Earth's atmosphere.

doc.title: Wikinews: 40th Berlin Christopher Street Day celebration attracts thousands: in pictures
doc.abstract: On Saturday, tens or hundreds of thousands of participants, reportedly, attended the 40th anniversary of the Berlin's celebration. The Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Transgender (LGBT) Pride is referred to as CSD in Germany and Switzerland.

doc.title: Wikinews: French footballer Lucas Digne joins Everton FC on five-year contract
doc.abstract: On Wednesday, English club Everton FC announced signing French footballer on a five-year contract from the Spanish LaLiga winners FC Barcelona. The 25-year old Frenchman's contract runs through June 2023.

doc.title: Wikinews: FC Barcelona signs Chilean footballer Arturo Vidal from Bayern
doc.abstract: On Friday, via a press release, FC Bayern Munich announced reaching an agreement with Spanish football club FC Barcelona for the transfer of Arturo Vidal. The Chilean midfielder was to sign a three-year contract with Barcelona after his medical examination.

doc.title: Wikinews: Spanish football: Sevilla signs Aleix Vidal from FC Barcelona
doc.abstract: On Saturday, announced the signing of Spanish defender Aleix Vidal from defending LaLiga champions FC Barcelona. Via their official website, Barcelona said they were to receive €8.

doc.title: Wikinews: Brazilian footballer Gabriel Jesus signs contract extension with Manchester City
doc.abstract: On Friday, English football club Manchester City announced Brazilian forward signed a contract extension adding two years to his contract with the club. Jesus's new contract runs until 2023.

doc.title: Wikinews: Football: Manchester City beats Chelsea 2-0 to win English Community Shield
doc.abstract: On Sunday, defending English winners Manchester City defeated London-based football club Chelsea FC 2–0 at the to win the 2018 . Sergio Agüero scored one goal in each half as Manchester City added another trophy to their collection.

doc.title: Wikinews: Real Madrid agrees with Chelsea FC to sign goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois
doc.abstract: Yesterday, English football club Chelsea FC announced reaching an agreement with Spanish-capital club Real Madrid to transfer Belgian goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois to Madrid. Real Madrid via their official website said Courtois "has signed for the club for the next six seasons.

doc.title: Wikinews: New South Wales, Australia government says entire state in winter 2018 drought
doc.abstract: On Wednesday, the New South Wales, Australia (DPI) reported fifteen percent of New South Wales, Australia (NSW) was in "intense drought", and the rest of the state "in drought" or "drought-affected". Farmers were reportedly running out of food for cattle and had to make difficult decisions about the collection times for their crops; food for cattle became harder to get, and more expensive.

doc.title: Wikinews: Singer Aretha Franklin, 'queen of soul', dies aged 76
doc.abstract: US singer Aretha Franklin died in her , Michigan home on Thursday morning, her publicist Gwendolyn Quinn stated on behalf of the family. According to the statement, the official cause of death was .

doc.title: Wikinews: Fossil genome shows hybrid of two extinct species of human
doc.abstract: A team of scientists has announced remains of a human girl from about 50 thousand years ago had one parent and one parent, two different species of humans, both species now extinct. The results, from tests in , Germany of bone from Siberia, Russia, were published on Wednesday in scientific journal .

doc.title: Wikinews: Brisbane, Australia Magistrates Court charges two cotton farmers with $20m fraud
doc.abstract: On Tuesday, two officers of cotton farming conglomerate Norman Farming in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia appeared in the Brisbane Magistrates Court for alleged fraud of the government. alleged over the past seven years the farmers submitted fraudulent claims to receive funding from Queensland's Department of Natural Resources, resulting in an approximately 20 million dishonest personal financial gain.

doc.title: Wikinews: Creativity celebrated at Fan Expo Canada 2018 in Toronto
doc.abstract: Fan Expo Canada ran in Toronto last weekend, from Thursday to Sunday, spread over both multi-storey buildings at the . The event is one of North America's largest pop culture events, with panels, product unveilings, screenings, an artists' alley, and celebrity autographs.

doc.title: Wikinews: US rapper Mac Miller dies at home in Los Angeles
doc.abstract: On Friday, was found dead in his bedroom at home in , Los Angeles, California, United States, according to reports. He was 26.

doc.title: Wikinews: NASA's TESS spacecraft reports its first exoplanet
doc.abstract: In findings released to the public on Monday through online site , astronomers reported they have already used data from the first photograph taken by National Aeronautics and Space Administration's (NASA's) (TESS) to locate an exoplanet. The planet, called , was spotted as it was transiting in front of its star, Pi Mensae ().

doc.title: Wikinews: Study suggests Mars hosted life-sustaining habitat for millions of years
doc.abstract: In a new study announced on Monday and available in the current volume of , an international team led by scientists from Brown University in the United States said the planet Mars once had the right water and temperatures to host simple life forms — just not on its surface. Mars's rocky, subterranean layer once, for some hundreds of millions of years, had enough water and reductants to support some of the same kinds of microbial communities seen on Earth.

Wikinews: UN Report on Global Warming calls for rapid 'unprecedented' changes globally to limit planetary warming to 1.5 degree C
doc.abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), a United Nations organization, released its (SR15) on Monday, during its 48th session held in , South Korea. In this report, the panel called for rapid "unprecedented" changes globally to limit planetary warming to 1.

doc.title: Wikinews: Manned Soyuz space mission aborts during launch
doc.abstract: Soyuz , a manned Russian space mission bound for the International Space Station (ISS) for a six-month stay, was forced to abort by a booster rocket failure Thursday morning. Rescue teams successfully recovered both crew members, Russian cosmonaut and United States astronaut , shortly after they landed safely in Kazakhstan.

doc.title: Wikinews: Israeli Supreme Court overturns expulsion of US student
doc.abstract: On Thursday, the Israeli ruled in favor of Lara Alqasem, a 22-year-old student who appealed an expulsion order, allowing her to remain in the country. She was refused entry upon arrival in Israel on October 2 at and threatened with deportation; Israeli authorities alleged that Alqasem supported a pro-Palestinian boycott against the state.

doc.title: Wikinews: U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren releases DNA test results, asks Donald Trump to make promised donation
doc.abstract: United States Senator Elizabeth Warren released to newspaper on Sunday, with public statement following on Monday, the results of a DNA test suggesting she has somewhere from 1/64 to 1/1024 ancestry. She took the test in response to a dare from U.

doc.abstract: At around 4:50 p.m.

doc.title: Wikinews: Jordan declares intent not to renew land lease to Israel
doc.abstract: On Sunday, King Abdullah II of Jordan announced his decision not to renew Israel's lease of two tracts of land on Jordan's side of the border. The lease, agreed upon in a , is set to expire next year.

doc.title: Wikinews: Simple animals could live in Martian brines: Wikinews interviews planetary scientist Vlada Stamenković
doc.abstract: Planetary scientist Vlada Stamenković of the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory and colleagues have developed a new chemical model of how oxygen dissolves in Martian conditions, which raises the possibility of oxygen-rich brines; enough, the work suggests, to support simple animals such as sponges. The model was published in on October 22.

doc.title: Wikinews: Technology giant Microsoft completes acquisition of GitHub
doc.abstract: On Friday, US-based technology giant Microsoft confirmed acquisition of software code hosting and version controlling website GitHub. The announcement was made by Microsoft via their official blog, which also mentioned was to become new Chief Executive Officer of GitHub.

doc.title: Wikinews: Syria's National Museum re-opens after six years of civil war
doc.abstract: In a ceremony attended by archaeologists and restoration specialists, authorities re-opened Syria's this Sunday, after six years of military conflict. Representatives of the government represented this as a milestone in the return to normalcy after recent victories in Syria's civil war.

doc.title: Wikinews: Football: Suárez scores hat-trick as Barça thrashes Real Madrid 5-1
doc.abstract: On Sunday, FC Barcelona defeated Spanish capital football club Real Madrid 5–1 in week 10 of LaLiga at the stadium. One goal each from Philippe Coutinho and Arturo Vidal and a by Luis Suárez guided Barcelona to victory, as the Catalan club reached 21 points, at the top of league table standings.

doc.title: Wikinews: 22nd annual ILGA-Europe conference meets in Brussels: in pictures
doc.abstract: On Saturday, the four day event of the 22nd Annual conference of (International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Intersex Association) ended which was hosted at the Belgian capital Brussels. According to the organisers, over 550 LGBTI activists attended this year's conference for LGBTI equality and human rights in Europe and .

doc.title: Wikinews: In pictures: thousands attend 16th annual Taiwan Pride
doc.abstract: On Saturday, over a hundred thousand people reportedly gathered in Taiwan's capital and participated in the 16th annual lesbian, gay, transgender and bisexual (LGBT) Pride. According to the organisers, about 137 thousand people participated in the largest LGBT Pride of Asia.

doc.title: Wikinews: Pakistan Supreme Court acquits Asia Bibi from blasphemy charges after eight years of confinement
doc.abstract: On Wednesday, the Pakistani Supreme Court acquitted Asia Bibi from charges. Asia Bibi is a Christian who was sentenced to death by hanging in November 2010 and remained in confinement on death row for the past eight years awaiting a final decision, reportedly much of it in solitary confinement.

doc.abstract: At 7:26 p.m.

doc.title: Wikinews: Storm causes building wall at Amazon.com warehouse to collapse
doc.abstract: On Friday, a storm caused a building to partially collapse in the Amazon Fulfillment Center at the warehouse of Amazon.com, a US-based online retailer, in south-east Baltimore, Maryland, United States.

doc.title: Wikinews: Ross Edgley swims around Great Britain for first time in history
doc.abstract: On Sunday, , aged 33, completed his 157-day (five-month) staged swim around mainland. He went ashore at , , Kent, England at 8:40 a.

doc.title: Wikinews: Mass graves of thousands of ISIL victims found, UN reports
doc.abstract: In a report issued on Tuesday, the United Nations announced the discovery of more than 200 mass graves in territory previously under the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL). The sites were located in northwestern Iraq, in , , , and provinces.

doc.title: Wikinews: Dozens of people killed in Mogadishu, Somalia car bombings near Sahafi Hotel
doc.abstract: On Friday at about 4 p.m.

doc.title: Wikinews: Merkel, Macron hold ceremonial meeting before 100th anniversary of World War I end
doc.abstract: On Saturday, the day before , German Chancellor Angela Merkel and French President held a ceremonial meeting at in northern France. There, 100 years prior, an was signed, ending fighting between the Allies and Germany in World War I.

doc.title: Wikinews: Israel and Palestinian militants agree to ceasefire after worst Gaza violence since 2014
doc.abstract: On Tuesday, Hamas and the Islamic Jihad Movement in Palestine, among other Palestinian militant groups in the Gaza Strip, announced a ceasefire agreement with Israel. The agreement was brokered by Egypt and the United Nations.

doc.title: Wikinews: Airbnb announces intent to remove Israeli West Bank settlement property listings
doc.abstract: On Monday, online rental firm announced its intent to remove housing listings in Israeli West Bank settlements. The decision would likely affect about 200 properties within the coming days.

doc.title: Wikinews: Wikinews attends 2018 Bangalore ComicCon
doc.abstract: On November 17 and November 18, Wikinews attended the 2018 Bangalore Comicbook Convention, in Karnataka, India. Beginning on Saturday morning, the ComicCon continued till Sunday.

doc.title: Wikinews: US National Climate Assessment warns of climate-related damages to economy, ecosystems, human health
doc.abstract: On Friday, the US presidential administration of Donald Trump released the (NCA4), a massive two-part congressionally mandated 1,656-page by the (USGCRP). The report, which focuses on the United States, warned consequences of climate change are increasing across the country.

doc.title: Wikinews: NASA's InSight Lander makes it to Mars
doc.abstract: On Monday shortly before noon US west coast time (2000 ), NASA's successfully touched down on on Mars. It sent a signal beep and image of the surface of Mars to the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in .

doc.title: Wikinews: Greek police arrest more than 60 people for gold smuggling
doc.abstract: On Wednesday, Greek police announced they arrested 63 people for gold smuggling. According to a report from Associated Press (AP), police seized cash, gold bars, and other items, totaling about two million euros (roughly 2.

doc.title: Wikinews: Investigation of Deutsche Bank headquarters spills into second day
doc.abstract: On Friday, German police investigators continued their previous day's search of the headquarters of in , Germany, for evidence of money laundering and other wrongdoing in connection to the group of leaked financial documents called the . A police spokesperson explained the roughly 170 searchers, including officers, prosecutors and tax experts, encountered such a volume of material the matter could not be concluded in one day.

doc.title: Wikinews: UK Parliament begins debate on Brexit deal
doc.abstract: On Tuesday, the United Kingdom Parliament started five days of debates ahead of a vote over Prime Minister Theresa May's deal to leave the European Union.

doc.title: Wikinews: Fire breaks out at Chester Zoo, England
doc.abstract: A fire occurred on Saturday at in , UK, in a building the zoo says is the largest indoor zoological exhibit in the UK, at 11:30 a.m.

doc.title: Wikinews: Australia now recognises West Jerusalem as Israeli capital, Prime Minister Scott Morrison announces
doc.abstract: On Saturday, Australian Prime Minister announced the national government's decision to recognise as Israeli capital, while reaffirming the nation's goal for two-state solution for Israel-Palestine conflict regarding authority of Jerusalem.

doc.title: Wikinews: Passengers evacuated at Prague airport after drawing of bomb found in plane
doc.abstract: On Sunday night in Prague, Czech Republic, 183 people on a flight arriving from Manchester, United Kingdom were evacuated after, reportedly, discovery in the aircraft's toilets of a picture of a bomb.

doc.title: Wikinews: Police warn new drone owners to obey law after disruption at UK's Gatwick Airport
doc.abstract: Police on Tuesday warned new owners of s to obey the law after Gatwick Airport, the second-largest airport in Britain, faced days of closure on account of drone sightings. About 150,000 travellers have had their plans affected.

doc.title: Wikinews: UK police locate missing Chinese teen Mei Chen, silent on details
doc.abstract: Seventeen-year-old Chinese student Mei Chen, who vanished from her host family's home in , England, was found safe and well on Thursday by police. Her host family suggested she was travelling to meet an unknown person from the Internet; Wikinews has contacted authorities to establish the circumstances, but has received no answers.

doc.title: Wikinews: Indonesia tsunami hits Sunda Strait after Krakatoa eruption
doc.abstract: On Saturday, a tsunami struck Indonesia's coastline at around 21:30 local time (1430 ). Indonesian officals suggested it was caused by an undersea landslide that followed the recent eruptions of , later receiving support from geological experts.

doc.title: Wikinews: US warns Spain of Christmas bus ramming plot in Barcelona
doc.abstract: Police in Barcelona, Spain yesterday were searching, according to reports, for a Moroccan man suspected of plotting an attack using a bus as a weapon during Christmas holidays. The United States State Department alerted the nation to the suspected plans.

doc.title: Wikinews: German government considers introducing mosque taxes, like church taxes
doc.abstract: On Wednesday, lawmakers of German ruling coalition parties — |de|German language|Christlich Demokratische Union Deutschlands}} (CDU), |de|German language|Sozialdemokratische Partei Deutschlands}} (SPD), and |de|German language|Christlich-Soziale Union in Bayern}} (CSU) — announced they were considering imposing new mandatory taxation Muslims would have to pay, which the government would distribute as funding to mosques. The lawmakers said this was a possible solution to stop funding and finance of the mosques in Germany from foreign countries and institutes.

doc.title: Wikinews: Scottish Borders minibus crash kills one, injures 23
doc.abstract: A minibus overturned on the A6089 road between and Carfraemill in the on Saturday night. The rural accident killed one man and injured 23 more.

doc.title: Wikinews: Magnitogorsk apartment building collapses after explosion, dozens dead
doc.abstract: An apartment building collapsed on Monday in , a city in the of Russia. A suspected gas leak led to an explosion, followed by the ten-storey building coming down.

doc.title: Wikinews: Male Magellanic penguins pine for pairings: Wikinews interviews biologist Natasha Gownaris
doc.abstract: In findings published earlier this month in , scientists from the and examine the reason for the plummeting numbers of female , Spheniscus magellanicus, that have been reported at the birds' breeding sites in South America over the past twenty years and more. Wikinews caught up with postdoctoral researcher and study co-author Natasha Gownaris to learn more.

doc.title: Wikinews: Nancy Pelosi again elected Speaker as 116th U.S. Congress sworn in
doc.abstract: Nancy Pelosi yesterday resumed the office of , being voted into the position by the incoming 116th United States Congress.

doc.title: Wikinews: Senator Ted Cruz proposes amendment to U.S. Constitution setting Congressional term limits
doc.abstract: On Thursday, former United States presidential candidate Senator Ted Cruz and fellow Republican Representative proposed to set lifetime limits for service in the Senate and House through amendment to the . It was co-sponsored by Senators Marco Rubio of Florida, of Utah, and of Georgia, all Republicans.

doc.title: Wikinews: Escape room fire kills five teen girls in Koszalin, Poland
doc.abstract: A fire yesterday afternoon killed five girls, all aged fifteen, at an the group was visiting to celebrate a birthday in , North Poland. Following the fire, which also seriously injured a man, authorities are performing checks on all the nation's escape rooms.

doc.title: Wikinews: Florida highway pileup, fire kills five children, two truck drivers
doc.abstract: A road accident followed by a fire on a Florida highway near Gainesville on Thursday killed five children in a church bus and two truck drivers. One and a car broke through the center guardrail before colliding with other vehicles; around 50 gallons of diesel fuel, officials said, spilled and ignited.

doc.title: Wikinews: President Trump says he 'can' and 'may' put US into state of emergency to build border wall
doc.abstract: United States Donald Trump said on Friday he can and may declare a national , which he said would allow him to act without approval from Congress and allocate funding for the construction of a wall along the country's border with Mexico. The US government is currently because the president and Congress could not agree on a national budget.

doc.title: Wikinews: Catalonia apartment block fire kills three, injures sixteen
doc.abstract: An apartment block caught fire on Saturday morning in , a Catalonian city around ten from Barcelona. The blaze killed three, including a 92-year-old woman, and injured sixteen, including a baby.

doc.title: Wikinews: Wikinews investigates disappearance of Indonesian cargo ship Namse Bangdzod
doc.abstract: In late December, Indonesian cargo ship Namse Bangdzod vanished in local waters. The tanker, around 1,150 and loaded with crude , had over ten crewmembers.

doc.title: Wikinews: Scientists report correlation between locations of Easter Island statues and water resources
doc.abstract: A United-States-based team of scientists released findings on Thursday about the large statues that dot the island of Rapa Nui, also called Easter Island. The study, published on Thursday in , employed quantitative to establish that the platforms, or , built to support the Easter Island statues, or , are usually located near sources of drinkable water.

doc.title: Wikinews: State-run bus crashes in Cuba en route to Havana, killing seven
doc.abstract: A bus operated by , which is run by the Cuban military's tourist section, crashed on Thursday between and . It was carrying a mix of locals and foreigners from Baracoa to Havana.

doc.title: Wikinews: Arrest made as mayor of Gdańsk, Poland stabbed on stage
doc.abstract: An individual has been arrested after Paweł Adamowicz, mayor of the Polish city of Gdańsk, was stabbed last night whilst on stage at a fundraising event. He died today.

doc.title: Wikinews: Iranian cargo plane crashes into Karaj houses
doc.abstract: A cargo plane, reported by local press as belonging to the Iranian military, crashed into houses in , near Tehran, the Iranian capital, yesterday. All but one of the sixteen on-board died; no deaths were reported on the ground, with local media reporting no-one was in the houses.

doc.title: Wikinews: Lion Air disaster: Crashed jet's voice recorder recovered from Java Sea
doc.abstract: The National Transportation Safety Committee of Indonesia on Monday announced the from has been recovered from the Java Sea. All 189 on the aircraft died when the flight came down last October.

doc.title: Wikinews: US study finds correlation between youth suicide, household gun ownership
doc.abstract: Professor of Boston University, co-author of a new study published in the on January 17, declared household gun ownership rates within the United States to be "the strongest single predictor of a state's youth suicide rate". Wikinews interviewed Siegel to learn more.

doc.title: Wikinews: Former U.S. intelligence agent Tony Mendez, architect of 'Argo' rescue, dies at 78
doc.abstract: Former United States Central Intelligence Agency agent died Saturday, aged 78, at a , Maryland assisted living facility. Mendez is known for organizing the safe return in 1980 of several U.

doc.title: Wikinews: Germany bans Mahan Air of Iran, citing 'security'
doc.abstract: Germany on Monday banned Iranian airline from flying in the European nation, with officials saying this is for security reasons.

doc.title: Wikinews: Car bomb ramming attack kills dozens at military base in Maidan Wardak, Afghanistan
doc.abstract: A car bomb was on Monday rammed into a military base in in the centre of Afghanistan's province. Dozens died in the attack, reportedly conducted by the Taliban.

doc.title: Wikinews: Bombs kill at least 20 at cathedral in Mindanao, Philippines
doc.abstract: Twin bombings yesterday struck the in Mindanao, Philippines. The second blast affected first responders following the first; between the two blasts, at least 20 were killed.

doc.title: Wikinews: Toronto serial killer Bruce McArthur pleads guilty to eight murders
doc.abstract: , from Toronto, Canada, on Tuesday admitted his guilt in eight murders. McArthur pleaded guilty to each crime at the Superior Court.

doc.title: Wikinews: Mokha, Yemen bomb kills photojournalist, at least five others
doc.abstract: A bombing was yesterday reported to have killed photojournalist Ziad al-Sharabi in the Red Sea port town of , Yemen. At least five other civilians reportedly also died in last night's attack; around twenty more, including colleague Faisal al-Thubhani, were injured.

doc.title: Wikinews: Report indicates Mexican monarch butterfly population at ten-year high, reasons unclear
doc.abstract: The announced on Wednesday the population counted over-wintering in Mexico was 144% greater than last year, with the highest overall population since the winter of 2006–2007. Scientists cautioned against an excess of optimism for the species.

doc.title: Wikinews: Paris court jails two police in high-profile rape case
doc.abstract: After a jury trial in Paris, two French police officers were found guilty on Thursday of raping a Canadian tourist in 2014. Both on Thursday received seven-year prison terms.

doc.title: Wikinews: Block of flats collapses in Aleppo, killing eleven
doc.abstract: State media on Saturday reported a war-damaged five-storey block of flats collapsed in a former rebel-held neighbourhood of Aleppo, Syria. The accident in district killed eleven, with a child the sole survivor.

doc.title: Wikinews: Bus carrying children overturns in Babyninsky, Russia; at least seven die
doc.abstract: A bus carrying children from Smolensk to on Sunday overturned in , Russia. At least seven, including four children, died.

doc.title: Wikinews: Nevada becomes first state in U.S. with majority-female legislature
doc.abstract: On Monday, Nevada became the first state in the United States to begin a state legislative session in which more than half of the elected officials were women, at 50.8 percent.

doc.title: Wikinews: Thai political party withdraws nomination of princess for prime minister
doc.abstract: On Saturday, Thailand's withdrew from using Princess as their candidate for prime minister in response to a statement from her younger brother, King . Shortly after she formally filed for candidacy, the palace issued a statement to the effect the king considered it inappropriate for Thai royals to run for elected office.

doc.title: Wikinews: Pioneering oceanographer Walter Munk dies of pneumonia in California
doc.abstract: The death of pioneering oceanographer was announced on Friday by the . He was 101 and died of in , California.

doc.title: Wikinews: Bishop Emeritus Dinualdo Gutierrez of Marbel, Philippines dies
doc.abstract: Roman Catholic Bishop Emeritus of the in the Philippines, 79, died early yesterday morning, in a hospital, according to the (CBCP). He would have been 80 on February 20.

doc.title: Wikinews: German migrant rescue charity renames ship after drowned Syrian toddler
doc.abstract: German migrant marine rescue charity on Sunday renamed their ship after , a three-year-old Syrian child who drowned offshore of Turkey. Relatives of the boy attended the renaming ceremony on the Spanish island of Majorca.

doc.title: Wikinews: Hotel fire kills at least seventeen in Karol Bagh, New Delhi
doc.abstract: The Hotel Arpit Palace in the Karol Bagh area of the Indian capital, New Delhi, caught fire yesterday morning. At least seventeen people died and 35 were rescued, according to officials, some of whom were hospitalised.

doc.title: Wikinews: Study indicates as great white shark disappears, living fossil moves in
doc.abstract: On Wednesday, scientists from the and published a study in , an on-line journal, documenting the disappearance of the (Carcharodon carcharias) from a specific area off the coast of South Africa. The study found that when the whites disappeared, a Jurassic-era predator called the (Notorhynchus cepedianus) moved in.

doc.title: Wikinews: Francis D'Souza, former Deputy Chief Minister of Goa, dies aged 64
doc.abstract: On Thursday, , previously the of the state of , , died. He had been suffering from .

doc.title: Wikinews: Fire kills nine, injures dozens in Chittagong, Bangladesh slum
doc.abstract: A fire yesterday morning destroyed at least 200 makeshift homes in a slum in Chittagong, a port city in Bangladesh. Officials said it killed nine people and injured at least 50 more.

doc.abstract: On Wednesday, nine men were jailed due to sexual abuse and rape of two teenage girls at a children's home in , England. A tenth defendant was found not-guilty.

doc.abstract: On Sunday, the SpaceX capsule successfully docked with the International Space Station in orbit around the Earth. doc.abstract: The roof of in French capital Paris caught fire yesterday. The spire and at least part of the roof, and at least part of the wooden frame, collapsed.

doc.abstract: Yesterday in California's criminal court, Judge Bernard Schwartz sentenced David and Louise Turpin to for torturing all but the youngest of their thirteen children.

doc.abstract: Wikinews attended the sixth annual Mini Maker Faire in Tyler, Texas, United States on Saturday. Similar to a giant science fair, the event featured a variety of science, engineering and technology projects and items.

doc.abstract: On Friday announced the United States was performing a criminal investigation of Ford's internal emission testing practices. doc.title: Wikinews: Scientific study suggests dinosaurs flapped their wings as they ran
doc.abstract: In findings published on Thursday in , scientists from China's and the reported bird flight may have evolved from wing-flapping by running dinosaurs. These findings support the hypothesis flight could have evolved up from the ground, in contrast to models in which active flapping flight evolved after gliding, a passive form of flight.

doc.title: Wikinews: Pope Francis instructs reporting of sexual abuse to higher church authorities
doc.abstract: On Thursday, Pope Francis announced new church law to mandate reporting sexual abuses to the church authorities. Per the decree signed by the leader of Roman Catholic Christianity, priests and nuns of the Catholic churches are expected to notify the higher church authorities, as a step to act on sexual abuse and its cover-up happening in the churches.

doc.title: Wikinews: Polish leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski promises stricter punishments for child abusers
doc.abstract: On Sunday, Polish leader Jarosław Kaczyński of the conservative publicly declared intent to impose stricter punishment for child sexual abuse. Kaczyński said the party was ready with amendments to the penal code for sentencing up to 30-year prison terms for child sexual abuse.

doc.title: Wikinews: Actor Doris Day dies at 97
doc.abstract: US singer, actor, and animal rights advocate died on Monday at her home in , California. Day made many studio albums, was awarded the , and rescued animals from Hurricane Katrina.

doc.title: Wikinews: Governor of US state of Alabama signs state anti-abortion measure
doc.abstract: On Wednesday in the state of , Governor signed the Alabama Human Life Protection Act, officially outlawing nearly all circumstances of in the state. This bill passed the Senate of the state on Tuesday.

doc.title: Wikinews: Taiwan's legislature first in Asia to legalize same-sex marriage
doc.abstract: On Friday the legislature of Taiwan, the , voted 66 to 27 to legalize , seven days ahead of the two-year deadline issued by the country's in 2017. This would make Taiwan the first country in Asia to legally recognize unions between same-sex couples.

doc.abstract: On Friday, thousands of Hong Kong protesters wearing black clothes, face masks, and helmets gathered around Hong Kong's principal police complex, blocking the exits as they chanted slogans and threw eggs. This comes after weeks of protests against a proposed change to Hong Kong's extradition law that would allow the Chinese government to remove people who had been accused of crimes from Hong Kong to the mainland.

doc.abstract: On Friday, on Route 2 in , New Hampshire, United States, a pickup truck and a group of ten motorcycles collided, the truck catching fire in the process. The incident left seven motorcyclists dead; the official cause of death reportedly was "blunt trauma.

doc.abstract: Acting via his lawyers, Volodoymyr Zhukovskyy, 23, pleaded not guilty on Tuesday to seven counts of in New Hampshire, United States. Zhukovskyy waived arraignment and did not physically appear in court.

doc.abstract: On Friday, United States Federal District Judge sentenced Ohio man , now 22, to life in prison without the possibility of parole for driving his car into a crowd of people who were counter-protesting against attending the August 2017 in , Virginia.

doc.abstract: On Friday, , the Prime Minister of Tunisia, signed a government decree banning anyone wearing a from entering a public institution or government offices. A niqab is a face-veil, which covers almost the entire face, and is commonly worn by Muslim females as a religious garment.

doc.abstract: Leaders of African Union (AU) member states met in , Niger's capital, for an AU summit where on Sunday Presidents Muhammadu Buhari of Nigeria and of Benin signed the (AfCFTA) agreement.

doc.abstract: John Paul Stevens, a former associate justice of the US Supreme Court, died yesterday at the age of 99, according to a statement released by the Supreme Court. Stevens died in the evening with his two daughters at his bedside at in Fort Lauderdale, Florida.

doc.abstract: The United States House of Representatives voted to hold two current Cabinet officers, and , in contempt of Congress, citing their refusal to disclose to Congress documents related to President Donald Trump's attempt to add a citizenship question to the 2020 census. The vote passed primarily along party lines, 230-to-198.

doc.abstract: In findings published Tuesday in Cornell University's by a team of scientists from the University of Montreal and a separate report published Wednesday in by a team from University College London (UCL), the presence of water vapour was confirmed in the atmosphere of , a planet circling a star in the . doc.abstract: Today at 10:30 (0930 ), the issued a ruling on the — a procedural suspension — of the Parliament of the United Kingdom until October 14. The court found that it could rule on the prorogation, and found the prorogation to be unlawful.

doc.abstract: Yesterday, oil facilities belonging to Saudi Arabia's state-owned Saudi Aramco were hit by multiple drone strikes in a pre-dawn raid. The attacks triggered major fires at a processing plant and an oil field, which state media said were under control.

doc.abstract: Yesterday, President Hassan Rouhani of Iran said if the goal is peace and security, then foreign powers should "get out of the region" as their presence could cause an arms race. He also announced a new security initiative for the Persian Gulf, the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz to be unveiled at the United Nations General Assembly later this week.

doc.abstract: Yesterday afternoon, Nancy Pelosi, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, announced that she would be launching an impeachment inquiry into the conduct of United States President Donald Trump. Pelosi had previously opposed impeachment proceedings.

doc.title: Wikinews: Singer-songwriter Robert Hunter dies, aged 78
doc.abstract: On Monday, US singer and lyricist died at his home in , California. His family's announcement of his death specified no cause, but, according to his agent, Hunter had undergone surgery recently.

doc.abstract: Friday, the United States House of Representatives issued a subpoena for documents from Secretary of State Mike Pompeo as part of its investigation into alleged misconduct by sitting President Donald Trump. On the same day, , the United States special envoy for Ukraine negotiations, resigned without public explanation.

doc.title: Wikinews: Former president of France Jacques Chirac dies aged 86
doc.abstract: This morning Jacques Chirac, who served as for twelve years, died at home in Paris, France, surrounded by family. He was 86.

doc.title: Wikinews: New South Wales decriminalizes abortion
doc.abstract: Yesterday, the of New South Wales (NSW), Australia voted to pass the "Reproductive Health Care Reform Bill 2019" which decriminalized abortion. Until the new legislation, NSW had the most restrictive anti-abortion law in Australia.

doc.abstract: On Thursday, Hatice Cengiz, fiancée of journalist , addressed reporters in New York, New York, calling for the killers of Khashoggi to be brought to justice. Cengiz traveled to New York for the United Nations (UN) General Assembly which took place this week.

doc.title: Wikinews: Brother of murdered Pakistani social media star sentenced to life
doc.abstract: On Friday in Pakistan, Mohammed Waseem, brother of social media personality and feminist , was sentenced for her murder to life in prison by a court in . Waseem confessed to killing his sister by strangling her in 2016 in what has widely been called an honor killing.

doc.title: Wikinews: World War II era plane crashes in Connecticut, US, killing at least seven
